review_notes: I read the whole target file and the related definitions in JetTrim.lean (trimWord, baseDirection, initialJet, cword_trim, trimWord_length). The target declares no simp lemmas, no simp attributes, no simp-set modifications and no local simp lemmas. Its simp calls are all local and terminal: `simp [p]`, `simp [he,p]`, `simpa [p,hj]`, `simp [p,(Finset.mem_erase.mp hj).1]` and `simpa [hm] using hb z`. The only unfolding is of the file-local `let p`. I found no competing rules, no rewrite in an unsuitable direction, no unwanted expansion and no credible cycle. One candidate was a simp lemma for `initialJet e f (i, none)` or `initialJet e f (i, some a)`. The proof closes that step with `rfl` after `rw [cword_trim, hzero i]`, so a simp lemma would not clearly help. The definitions of `trimWord` and `baseDirection` are not tagged simp in JetTrim.lean, and the target uses them only through explicit rewrites. I did not run Lean, so I cannot rule out minor simp-robustness issues. I found none that the sources support.
